title: Debug: The Top Earner's Name Doesn't Match Their Salary
description:
This is meant to report, per department, the name and salary of that department's **top earner**. It runs without error and returns one row per department — but the name shown is often not actually the person earning that MAX salary. Find the bug and fix it.

Name the columns `department`, `top_earner` and `top_salary`. Return the result in any order.
solutionSql:
SELECT d.name AS department, e.name AS top_earner, e.salary AS top_salary
FROM departments d
JOIN employees e ON e.dept_id = d.id
WHERE e.salary = (SELECT MAX(e2.salary) FROM employees e2 WHERE e2.dept_id = d.id);
hint: SQLite allows selecting a column that's neither aggregated nor in GROUP BY (most other databases reject this outright) — but the value you get back is from an arbitrary row in the group, not necessarily the one MAX() came from. Join back to find the actual row where salary equals the max instead.
schemaSql:
CREATE TABLE departments (
  id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  name TEXT,
  location TEXT
);

CREATE TABLE employees (
  id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  name TEXT,
  title TEXT,
  salary INTEGER,
  dept_id INTEGER,
  manager_id INTEGER,
  hire_date TEXT
);

tests.name: Department with no employees
Employees with NULL department and NULL salary
Single employee, single department
tests.seedSql:
INSERT INTO departments VALUES (1,'Engineering','Austin');
INSERT INTO employees VALUES (1,'Solo','Engineer',100000,1,NULL,'2022-04-01');

tests.name: Duplicate names and same hire dates
Zero and negative salaries, boundary dates
Max earner has a lower id — arbitrary row is wrong
tests.seedSql:
INSERT INTO departments VALUES (1,'Engineering','Austin'),(2,'Sales','Denver');
INSERT INTO employees VALUES (1,'LowEarner','E',50000,1,NULL,'2020-01-01'),(2,'TopEarner','E',150000,1,1,'2020-01-01');

tests.name: Single employee per department — no ambiguity
tests.seedSql:
INSERT INTO departments VALUES (1,'Engineering','Austin'),(2,'Sales','Denver');
INSERT INTO employees VALUES (1,'Ava','E',100000,1,NULL,'2020-01-01'),(2,'Eve','E',90000,2,NULL,'2020-01-01');

tests.name: Tie for max salary — both should show same name
tests.seedSql:
INSERT INTO departments VALUES (1,'Engineering','Austin');
INSERT INTO employees VALUES (1,'A','E',150000,1,NULL,'2020-01-01'),(2,'B','E',150000,1,1,'2020-01-01'),(3,'C','E',120000,1,1,'2020-01-01');

tests.seedSql:
INSERT INTO departments VALUES (1,'Engineering','Austin'),(2,'Ghost','Nowhere');
